📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s a familiar interruption that comes with shopping online: you’ve found what you want, you’re ready to check out, and the store asks you to sign in. Was this the account with your usual password? Did you change it last time? Is it easier to reset it again?

Sources indicate that for Black Friday, Proton Pass Plus and Pass Family are both 60% off their regular monthly pricing with a one-year subscription, while Proton Unlimited is 50% off. Pass Plus starts at $1.99 per month, billed annually, making this a good opportunity to get your passwords — and a few other important parts of your digital life — organized.

The problem with strong passwords isn’t understanding why you need them; it’s keeping track of a different one for every account.

That’s useful whether you’re creating an account for a single purchase or signing into a service you use every day.

Recent findings suggest that unique passwords also help limit the fallout from a data breach. If a retailer exposes your login credentials, using a different password elsewhere means those same credentials won’t unlock your other accounts.

With unlimited logins and encrypted vaults that sync across devices, Proton Pass lets you keep those details together as you move between your phone and computer.

Proton Pass is available for practically every platform, from Chrome and Firefox on the web to native macOS, Windows, and Linux apps to, of course, iOS and Android. This makes it trivially easy to access your passwords, passkeys, and API credentials wherever you find yourself.

Black Friday shopping often leaves something behind long after the packages arrive: a steady stream of promotional emails from stores you barely remember visiting.

Proton Pass includes unlimited hide-my-email aliases, giving you an alternative to handing out your real address every time you create an account.

It has been revealed that an alias is an extra email address that forwards messages to your normal inbox. You can give it to a shopping website and still receive your order confirmations and delivery updates, without sharing the underlying address you use for everything else.

According to recent reports, if that alias starts receiving spam, you can switch it off. Your real email address stays the same, and you don’t have to update all your other accounts.

Recent findings suggest that it’s a practical way to put some distance between your primary inbox and the websites you’re trying for the first time. A separate alias for each service also gives you more control: you can stop messages arriving through one address without disrupting the others.

Passwords are only part of what’s worth keeping in a secure, accessible place.

Industry observers note that proton Pass also stores notes, credit card details, and other confidential information in end-to-end encrypted vaults. That makes it useful for the small, everyday moments when you need something sensitive and don’t want to go looking for it.

When you’re booking a flight, saved passport details let you look up the information you need without digging through a drawer halfway through the reservation.

When you’re shopping online, saved card details mean you don’t have to leave the checkout page to find your wallet.

Industry observers note that when you’re traveling, keeping a digital copy of an important document within reach gives you a convenient reference while you’re away from home. It doesn’t replace an original document where one is required, but it can save you from searching through scattered files and messages.

Pass Plus also includes a built-in two-factor authenticator, Dark Web Monitoring, and secure link and vault sharing. Those features give you more ways to manage access to your accounts and share sensitive information when you need to.

Pass Plus is the straightforward choice for one person who wants password generation, autofill, unlimited aliases, and secure storage.

Industry observers note that pass Family includes six Pass Plus accounts and a family admin panel. If several people in your household need a password manager, it’s worth considering rather than setting everyone up with separate subscriptions.

Proton Unlimited bundles Pass with Proton VPN, Proton Mail, Proton Drive, and more, including 500 GB of cloud storage. It’s the option to consider if you also want a VPN, encrypted email, and cloud storage alongside your password manager.

A password manager isn’t the most conspicuous Black Friday purchase, but it’s one you can put to work immediately: the next account you create, the next password you forget, or the next time a checkout asks for details you don’t have handy.

Proton’s offers are available to fresh users and include a 30-day money-back guarantee.

At $600, the Pixel 10 is this year’s no-brainer Black Friday smartphone deal

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Phones have gotten a lot more expensive over the last year or so, and it’s a trend we’re expecting to get worse before it can get better.
  • While buying year-old hardware typically comes with some pretty deep sacrifices between generations, that’s not particularly true with the Pixel 10 this year.
  • So what are you giving up that matters?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Phones have gotten a lot more expensive over the last year or so, and it’s a trend we’re expecting to get worse before it can get better. If you’re in the market for an upgrade, this year’s Black Friday might be one of the final truly good times to buy a new device, and for just $600, last year’s Pixel 10 should be high on your list.

While buying year-old hardware typically comes with some pretty deep sacrifices between generations, that’s not particularly true with the Pixel 10 this year. From a hardware perspective, nearly everything is either identical or close enough to not particularly matter. Its design and display are all but unchanged, Qi2-ready magnets come on both models, and both devices are built with the same level of battery longevity in mind. And much to the chagrin of many a Pixel die-hard, Tensor G5 and Tensor G6 are practically interchangeable.

So what are you giving up that matters? When the Pixel 11 arrived, software features made up the bulk of this list, but with last week’s Pixel Drop, a lot of the gaps between these two generations have been closed. Gemini Intelligence with Rambler, app automation, and more are in the process of rolling out to existing Pixel 10 users, and latest features like Create My Widget arrived on the Pixel 10 and 11 at the exact same time. From a software perspective — Google’s bread and butter, in my eyes — the only big sacrifice comes from the year of software support that’s already complete, leaving you with just six instead of seven.

Sources indicate that realistically, the camera is the one place you’re likely to feel a difference. The Pixel 10 was the first non-Pro device in Google’s Tensor era to ship with a telephoto lens, but it came with some big sacrifices. The main sensor is effectively an A-series lens, and taken together, the entire package might leave something to be desired. It’s far from a bad camera though — I used it as my main shooter through most of its lifecycle — and while the Pixel 11 did get some upgrades here, I think real shutterbugs would be better off looking at Google’s Pro lineup anyway. You’ll also lose out on things like HiLight, though really, are you missing that much?

Industry observers note that what makes this deal so good is really its place in the market, not as a direct comparison to the newer Pixel 11. For $600, Google’s competition is going to have a hard time competing with the value the Pixel 10 delivers. Hell, even Google might find it difficult to compete in the coming months; at full price, $600 is what the Pixel 10a goes for now, a decidedly less-impressive device compared to this model. No, this is a flagship smartphone through and through, and for $600, you’re effectively guaranteeing a reliable, powerful smartphone experience from now until 2032 — hopefully enough time for this whole RAM crisis to finally simmer down a bit.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Honor Watch 6 Pro has a 5,500-nit OLED display, ceramic bezel, 18-day battery life, and costs less than it looks.

In a recent development, in the world of athletic smartwatches, it isn’t often that you could mistake one for a luxury watch, but Honor seems to want to flip all that on its head with the Honor Watch 6 Pro. Just take a look at this excerpt from the manufacturer’s press release:.

Framing this brilliant display is a Precision Nanocrystalline Ceramic bezel crafted through a 1400°C high-temperature integrated sintering process, delivering a delicate texture and rich visual depth.

Inspired by modernist architecture, its diamond-cut octagonal rotatable crown features a dual-layer horizontal and vertical cut, complemented by a side button for intuitive navigation.

Recent findings suggest that that sounds pretty wild to me, and it’s backed up by specs that sound just as legit, too. On top is a 1.5-inch LTPO Tandem AMOLED display that outputs 5,500-nit peak brightness. Underneath is a bevy of fresh sensors called the Intelligent Sense System, which Honor claims combines “multi-wavelength monitoring, multi-optical path patrol technology, and anti-interference glass technology to reach deep skin layers.”.

Recent findings suggest that runners will be pleased to know that the Honor Watch 6 Pro not only incorporates a dual-band GPS, but combines it with a “star-pointing 3-antenna design” and an AI fusion algorithm, which should deliver ultra-accurate tracking in any location and no matter how you hold your wrist. Despite its luxury looks, this one tracks over 120 sports modes, including Honor’s Professional Running Coach feature, which tracks running posture, lactate threshold, heart rate targets, and keeps you on pace with real-time voice coaching.

During sports modes like Badminton, the watch can identify more than six types of swings, and Honor says other sports modes can deliver similarly detailed statistics. The watch is 5ATM, IP68, IP69, and IP69K water-and-dust-resistant rated, plus it integrates directly with Strava so you can pull all your fitness data together.

Honor is incorporating a newly introduced wrist twist gesture system this time around, letting you use gestures to perform actions hands-free. The watch is rated at 10 days of battery life on a single charge in regular usage mode, while endurance mode will stretch that to 18 days. Pre-sales begin today, November 19, and run until December 31, when the watch is expected to launch, starting at €279/£229 for early bird pricing. After launch, the retail MSRP starts at €379/£329.

PENN’s Interactive revenue rise rests on partner taxes as gaming revenue slips 2.1%

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (594 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readwrite

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • PENN Entertainment's online segment grew revenue in the third quarter, but the gain came from passed-through partner gaming taxes, not from players.
  • Other revenues carried the whole of the Interactive segment’s third-quarter gain at PENN Entertainment.
  • This pattern places PENN within the slowing-iGaming-growth story running through this week’s US operator reports.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

PENN Entertainment's online segment grew revenue in the third quarter, but the gain came from passed-through partner gaming taxes, not from players. The segment now needs a positive fourth quarter to reach a full-year target that has already been lowered.

Other revenues carried the whole of the Interactive segment’s third-quarter gain at PENN Entertainment. Segment revenue rose to $348.4 million from $297.7 million, while the third-party partner gaming-tax amounts booked there climbed to $191.4 million from $139.5 million a year earlier. Online gaming revenue itself fell 2.1% to $126.6 million from $129.3 million, as iCasino growth was offset by lower sports betting handle.

This pattern places PENN within the slowing-iGaming-growth story running through this week’s US operator reports.

The nine-month figures show the same reliance on the gross-up. Interactive revenue reached $1,056.0 million, up from $903.9 million. The tax gross-up within it rose to $562.7 million from $405.6 million.

The group as a whole had a stronger quarter. Total revenue was $1,840.0 million. Net income came in at $32.6 million, against a $865.1 million net loss a year earlier. PENN also raised its full-year retail guidance to $5.89 billion in revenue and $1.973 billion in adjusted EBITDAR, increases of $16 million and $10 million.

Profitability is improving faster than revenue. The Interactive adjusted EBITDA loss for the first nine months shrank to $38.7 million from $227.6 million. PENN attributes that mainly to lower marketing, general and administrative, and labor costs.

Expansion has weighed on the quarter. PENN introduced theScore Bet, theScore Casino and standalone Hollywood iCasino apps in Alberta on July 13, 2026. Excluding that third-quarter launch investment, Interactive adjusted EBITDA improved quarter over quarter throughout 2026, management said on the earnings call.

Recent findings suggest that the standalone Hollywood iCasino brand is central to the blueprint. It posted record quarterly revenue in the second quarter. PENN is now leaning on its US growth, and on steady trends through October, to support the full-year Interactive target. That makes the brand a test for whether a mid-tier US online casino can turn profitable.

Recent findings suggest that the target itself has moved. In February, PENN guided the segment to breakeven adjusted EBITDA for 2026, which it described as a $268 million improvement from 2025. The cost of the Alberta launch is now built into a weaker outlook.

PENN Entertainment CEO Jay Snowden discussed the potential of more Canadian provinces launching iGaming on an earnings call today.

In the last month, Quebec, Newly introduced Brunswick, and Nova Scotia have all shown interest in exploring commercial online gambling.https://t.co/8WqAPfw9LY.

— Tom Nightingale (@TNightingaming) November 5, 2026.

Recent findings suggest that land-based trends offer some support. CEO Jay Snowden noted PENN’s own Pennsylvania gaming revenue in October posted stronger year-over-year growth than in any other month of 2026. Most of that growth came in the second half of the month, after skill games were shut down. In his view, the midterm results could help PENN further by weakening support for skill-game machines.

It has been revealed that the online segment still has to deliver. Reaching the revised target depends on Interactive turning its third-quarter loss into positive adjusted EBITDA in the fourth quarter.

Industry observers note that A few years ago, renting a VPS meant signing up to be a part-time sysadmin. You’d SSH into a blank Ubuntu prompt and lose a Saturday to Nginx configs and firewall rules before writing a single line of your actual project.

In a recent development, in 2026, three things have changed. What we build has changed: AI coding tools turn weekend ideas into working apps, and AI agents need a machine that stays on after your laptop closes. Who runs servers has changed: you can now ask an AI agent in your terminal to set up a reverse proxy, close a port or work out why something broke. And what servers cost has changed: the AI boom is soaking up the world’s memory supply, and hosting prices are rising with it.

So I bought the smallest Hostinger VPS plan, deployed a Node.js app in Docker, and handed the DevOps work to Hostinger Agent, the AI assistant built into the dashboard.

Below is what that felt like step by step and whether it’s worth locking in a price before they climb further.

Recent findings suggest that most VPS hosting for developers now falls into four buckets. They all run on the same kind of machine; what changes is how much RAM you give them.

Apps built with AI coding tools. Claude Code and Cursor get you to a working Node.js or Python app fast, then leave you wondering where to put it. A VPS gives you one fixed monthly bill instead of usage-based pricing. If you want push-to-deploy, Hostinger offers Ubuntu templates with Coolify or Dokploy preinstalled.

AI agents and automations that run 24/7. For most people, a “VPS for AI” means a CPU box that never sleeps, not a GPU. Think n8n workflows, a scheduled scraper, or your own agent in a Docker container. Hostinger even has an “Ubuntu 24.04 with Claude Code” template: SSH in, run claude /login, and the agent keeps working after you close your laptop.

Sources indicate that APIs, backends and databases for side projects. A Postgres instance, a Redis cache and a small API behind a reverse proxy fit comfortably on a mid-sized proposal. You pick the versions, the extensions and the backup schedule.

Client sites and stores. Freelancers outgrow shared hosting when one client needs a custom PHP extension or a WooCommerce store starts to crawl. A VPS with cPanel or Plesk, or a WordPress or WooCommerce template, keeps client work isolated and under your control.

If you’d rather not build anything from scratch, the Docker Manager catalog listed 1,017 one-click templates when I checked, including 93 under AI/ML and 162 under Developer tools.

For this Hostinger VPS review, the question I cared about was simple: how long from “Choose blueprint” to an app on the internet? On KVM 1, the entry plan, it was about 12 minutes. Here’s each step with rough timings.

I went with KVM 1: 1 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 50 GB NVMe storage and 4 TB of bandwidth. On the Black Friday deal it costs $6.49/mo, paid upfront as $155.76 for 24 months, and renews at $11.99/mo.

You choose the server’s location and what to install during checkout, alongside your billing details. The location picker shows estimated latency for each data centre; mine indicated about 80 ms.

Industry observers note that install options come in three tabs: Plain OS, Control panel and Applications. I picked plain Ubuntu 26.04 LTS to see how much work the AI would take off my hands. A daily backup add-on is offered, but weekly backups are already included.

According to recent reports, the five-minute estimate was about right. The “you’re ready” screen then gives you two ways in: the VPS dashboard, or a pre-filled ssh root@ command. It also offers a free domain for a year to use as the server’s hostname.

The overview shows the OS, strategy, CPU, RAM, disk and bandwidth at a glance, with Docker Manager, Backups & Monitoring, Security and DNS Manager in the side menu.

Every server also gets a hostname under hstgr.cloud (mine was srvXXXXXXX.hstgr.cloud), which came in handy later for SSL. I’ve masked my hostname as srvXXXXXXX throughout and blurred IP addresses in the screenshots.

In a recent development, plain Ubuntu doesn’t ship with Docker. Open Docker Manager in hPanel and it installs Docker for you with one click. From there you can deploy apps from a Compose file, a repository URL or the one-click catalog.

Click Web console and you’re logged in as root in a browser tab, with Hostinger Agent in a panel beside it. You don’t need an SSH client or keys. The login banner flagged 33 pending updates, 23 of them security fixes; more on that later. A quick docker --version confirmed Docker 29.9.3 was ready.

Here’s the whole app: a tiny HTTP server with a health check, and a Dockerfile on Node.js 24, a supported LTS line.

Then build it, run it and check it:.

It has been revealed that the build took 8.3 seconds, including pulling node:24-alpine, and the health check answered straight away. The --restart unless-stopped flag brings the container back after a crash or reboot, which I tested later.

That’s a working app, but on plain HTTP, on a high port, with no TLS. Getting it production-ready is the DevOps part I handed to the AI.

It has been revealed that an AI-managed VPS isn’t the same as a traditional managed VPS. You still get a self-managed server with full root access, but Hostinger Agent does the work you’d normally do yourself. Agent (previously called Kodee) is an MCP-powered assistant that lives in the dashboard and beside the AI web terminal, and it’s included at no extra cost. You can also connect Claude or Cursor to your server through Hostinger’s MCP server.

I gave it three tasks in plain English.

My prompt: “Check that Docker is installed, then set up a reverse proxy with a free SSL certificate so my demo-app container (port 3000) is served at https://srvXXXXXXX.hstgr.cloud.”.

According to recent reports, it started by looking around: the Docker and Compose versions, which ports were in use, whether a web server was already running, and the OS release. Then it installed Caddy from Caddy’s official repository, configured the proxy and made sure ufw allowed web traffic.

It read Caddy’s logs to confirm the Let’s Encrypt certificate, which arrived in about 6 seconds. Finally it tested its own work: HTTPS returned 200, and plain HTTP returned a 308 redirect. The whole task took about two minutes.

It has been revealed that to give it a real fault, I ran docker stop demo-app and reloaded the site. Then I asked why it was returning a 502 and to fix it.

Sources indicate that in a single command, it checked the container state (Exited (137)) and searched Caddy’s logs, where it found connect: connection refused on port 3000. It restarted the container, confirmed /health and HTTPS were back, and even pointed to my docker stop in the terminal history. It also explained that --restart unless-stopped covers crashes and reboots, but not a manual stop.

Recent findings suggest that A tip it didn’t mention: exit code 137 means Docker had to force-kill the container, because Node running as PID 1 ignores SIGTERM. Add --init to docker run for clean, instant shutdowns.

Sources indicate that this was the most impressive answer. ufw already allowed only those three ports, but Agent noticed port 3000 was still reachable from the internet, because Docker-published ports bypass ufw rules.

Sources indicate that it recreated the container bound to 127.0.0.1:3000, so the app is only reachable through Caddy, and confirmed with an external port check. It left DNS, time sync and Caddy’s local admin port running, explaining that stopping them would break DNS and time sync.

Industry observers note that then I asked it to reboot the server. First it checked that Docker and Caddy start on boot and that the container’s restart policy was set, then it rebooted. The site came back over HTTPS without any help from me.

Nothing I asked for was destructive, so Agent just got on with it: the firewall change, the container rebuild and the reboot all ran without a confirmation prompt.

In a recent development, the Agent panel says so upfront, noting that terminal commands can run without one. For destructive actions such as reinstalling the OS or restoring a backup, Hostinger’s FAQ says Agent always asks for confirmation first.

One thing worth knowing: to close port 3000, Agent removed and recreated my container. That was harmless for a stateless demo, but a container that keeps data without a volume would lose it. Take a snapshot before big jobs, and keep the panel in view.

Here are the four intends at their Black Friday rates for a 24-month term.

For scale, here’s what my test used. With the Node app, Docker and Caddy all running, KVM 1 had 3.3 GB of its 4 GB RAM still available, and the app container itself used about 65 MB.

In a recent development, so 4 GB is plenty for one or two small apps. Move to 8 GB on KVM 2 once you add Coolify, a database, or n8n with its own Postgres, because those are the services that eat memory.

It has been revealed that finding a cheap VPS got harder in 2026, because memory got expensive. AI data centres are buying up DRAM, and hosts are passing the cost on. In April 2026, Hetzner raised cloud server prices by up to 37%, citing hardware costs, then raised prices again in June. On the same April date, OVHcloud’s entry VPS went from $4.90 to $7.60, a 55% jump. Nobody can promise where VPS prices go next, but the trend this year has been up.

Sources indicate that this is how Hostinger’s Black Friday pricing works. You pay upfront for 12 or 24 months, and the 24-month term gives the lowest monthly rate. Your price is fixed for that whole term. After that, it renews at the standard rate.

It has been revealed that on KVM 2, for example, you pay $210.96 today (the $8.79/mo rate) for 24 months, and it renews at $14.99/mo after that. Do the maths on the renewal before you commit, not just the headline rate.

Second Circuit denies Kalshi and Coinbase interim relief against Latest York and Connecticut

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Second Circuit has refused to shield Kalshi and Coinbase from Upcoming York and Connecticut while their appeals proceed.
  • A federal appeals panel has left Kalshi and Coinbase without interim protection in two Northeastern states.
  • The ruling came a few hours after the panel heard lawyers for Kalshi, Coinbase, the CFTC, New York and Connecticut.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Second Circuit has refused to shield Kalshi and Coinbase from Upcoming York and Connecticut while their appeals proceed. The ruling lets both states press state-court cases against the companies' sports event contracts and deepens a circuit split headed for the Supreme Court.

A federal appeals panel has left Kalshi and Coinbase without interim protection in two Northeastern states. The Second Circuit found that the companies had not made the showing needed for an injunction pending appeal. The order did not say which part of that showing they failed to meet.

The ruling came a few hours after the panel heard lawyers for Kalshi, Coinbase, the CFTC, New York and Connecticut. The court took up Kalshi’s two appeals together with Coinbase’s appeal of Judge Oliver’s August decision. That decision allowed Connecticut to keep pursuing its claim that Coinbase’s sports event contracts are illegal gambling.

The order lets both states keep enforcing their gambling laws. They are pursuing state-court suits to force the sports event contracts offline. Gaming attorney Daniel Wallach called the ruling a major win for both states. He said one remand order now separates them from returning the cases to state court and seeking preliminary injunctions there.

Kalshi had already lost at the district level. Federal courts refused it a preliminary injunction in Newly introduced York in July and in Connecticut in August. On July 31, 2026, New York sued KalshiEX, accusing it of running an illegal gambling operation through its prediction market. Attorney General Letitia James had sued Coinbase and Gemini in April 2026 on similar illegal gambling claims.

In a recent development, the stakes in Fresh York are high. InGame reported that the state case seeks billions of dollars in damages, and that the CFTC has told Kalshi to disobey the state-court order if it ever takes effect.

It has been revealed that connecticut moved earlier. In December 2025, the Gaming Division of its Department of Consumer Protection ordered Kalshi and two other sites to stop offering unlicensed online sports wagering. On August 26, 2026, Attorney General William Tong, Consumer Protection Commissioner Bryan T. Cafferelli and Gov. Ned Lamont revealed a lawsuit to stop Kalshi offering unlicensed sports wagers in the state. Gov. Kathy Hochul, James, Tong and Lamont each won re-election on the day the order was issued.

The decision joins a lengthening list of circuit court rulings siding with states against prediction markets in 2026. It cuts against Kalshi’s argument that its contracts are “swaps” that only the CFTC can regulate. That argument prevailed at the Third Circuit, which ruled that New Jersey cannot regulate sports bets on prediction markets.

Nine federal judicial rulings within the Second Circuit have now gone against Kalshi, Coinbase and/or the CFTC in efforts to block state gambling enforcement through emergency or preliminary relief.

That includes today’s Second Circuit ruling denying Kalshi’s….

— Daniel Wallach (@WALLACHLEGAL) November 4, 2026.

Sources indicate that the federal regulator has also gone to court against states. On April 2, 2026, the CFTC sued Arizona, Connecticut and Illinois over their actions against CFTC-registered designated contract markets. On April 24, 2026, it sued Fresh York in the Southern District of New York. It asked that court to declare that federal law gives it exclusive authority over event contracts. It also asked for a permanent bar on the state enforcing preempted laws.

The outcome matters for state sportsbook markets and for the reach of CFTC jurisdiction. With the circuits now split, attention turns to Washington. New Jersey’s petition seeks review of the Third Circuit’s April 6, 2026 decision in case 25-1922. Kalshi is preparing to file its response to that petition.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Charlie Geren filed a constitutional amendment on the first filing day of Texas's 2027 session that would let voters decide on casinos and sports betting.
  • It has been revealed that texas lawmakers have their first gambling-expansion measures of the 2027 session.
  • Industry observers note that the resolution would require lawmakers to limit casinos to a capped number of facilities statewide.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that rep. Charlie Geren filed a constitutional amendment on the first filing day of Texas's 2027 session that would let voters decide on casinos and sports betting. A Democratic House and a supportive lieutenant governor-elect improve its odds, but a two-thirds Senate vote and a fight over the Senate's leadership stand in the way.

It has been revealed that texas lawmakers have their first gambling-expansion measures of the 2027 session. Rep. Charlie Geren, a Fort Worth Republican, filed House Joint Resolution 52 on November 9, the first day of bill filing, and Democratic Sen. Carol Alvarado filed a Senate resolution on casinos and sports betting, SJR 11, the same day. Voters would get the final say on a constitutional change giving lawmakers the power to permit and oversee casinos and sports betting.

Industry observers note that the resolution would require lawmakers to limit casinos to a capped number of facilities statewide. Initial license terms would run at least 40 years. The Legislature would decide where sports betting could take place. The ballot wording would describe licensing, application fees and a tax on casino and sports wagering revenue at a limited number of locations.

Geren framed a statewide vote as the end of the debate either way. A rejection at the ballot box would close the question permanently, he mentioned.

The political ground has moved since Geren’s last attempt. Democrats won control of the Texas House in the November 3 election. Republicans held on to the Senate. As a state representative, Goodwin backed the 2023 gambling measure. The office she won was held by Dan Patrick, who blocked gambling expansion for years.

Recent findings suggest that the constitutional route keeps the bar high. An amendment needs two-thirds of both chambers, then a majority of voters. Approved amendments go on the November ballot after the session ends. In 2023, online sports betting passed the House with 101 votes. Geren’s casino resolution reached only 92. The casino measure fell short of the threshold that the betting measure cleared.

According to recent reports, the Senate is the harder test. Republicans control the chamber, and any amendment needs two-thirds support there. On November 9, Patrick urged Republican senators on conservative radio to strip Goodwin of her powers as Senate president before she takes office. Her influence over the chamber, including any gambling bill, now hangs on that fight.

Goodwin has signaled a conciliatory approach. Her transition team said she wants to work with Republican senators and believes Texas is “best served by a deliberative, collaborative body.”.

According to recent reports, texas Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick, arguably the casino and sports betting industry's biggest boogeyman in the Lone Star State, will leave office next year. What comes next in a crucial 2027 for the largest remaining state without major casino gaminghttps://t.co/u6WLlaAj3S.

— Ryan Butler (@butlerbetstrade) November 4, 2026.

Industry money has struggled to change the Republican map. In the March primaries, anti-gambling incumbents beat challengers backed by the Las Vegas Sands-funded Texas Sands PAC and Texas Defense PAC, to which Miriam Adelson had given $9 million. Even so, Texas Sands PAC has pledged to keep investing in and organizing for Texas candidates who favor bringing casino gambling to the state.

In a recent development, that leaves Geren’s measure dependent on a Senate whose leadership is still contested. A simple majority could strip Goodwin’s powers once the chamber reconvenes in January.

  • Patch: Google replied on Reddit to “clear up some confusion” about the Help Center page.
  • Noto 3D emoji, with its high-resolution bitmap approach, uses less than 220 MB of storage versus the previous 2D vector font that comes in at around 3 MB.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google introduced 3D emoji on Pixel this year, and has just detailed the minimum specifications required to get them on your Android phone.

Patch: Google replied on Reddit to “clear up some confusion” about the Help Center page. The listed storage and RAM requirements refer to the “automatic background download via Google Play services on eligible Android 17 devices that didn’t ship with the 3D font preinstalled.” The support article did not make that distinction.

Noto 3D emoji, with its high-resolution bitmap approach, uses less than 220 MB of storage versus the previous 2D vector font that comes in at around 3 MB.

During installation, Google Play services temporarily needs a bit of extra headroom to copy the file into place before immediately clearing its download cache.

Meanwhile, Google noted RAM usage is “minimal & transient” as “Android doesn’t load the 3D emoji font file into RAM.” The support page listed 6 GB as a “cutoff to ensure lower-memory devices stay on the lightweight ~3 MB 2D vector font.”.

Noto 3D emoji goes from vector-based 2D emoji to a high-resolution bitmap font. This results in “high-resolution designs” for emoji “with more texture and dimension to characters and icons.” Google has an FAQ section about why the latest emoji might look low resolution:.

According to recent reports, vector vs. bitmap rendering: Older Android emoji used 2D vector graphics, which scale infinitely to any size without losing resolution. The 3D emoji are bitmap graphics, which are pre-rendered pixel-based images. When these images are scaled up by an app or zoomed in, the pixels stretch, which can cause a softer or lower-resolution appearance.

The Google support article published this week lists the minimum specs your Android device must have to get 3D emoji:.

The last two bullet points are rather surprising. In fact, Google even lists instructions for checking how much memory and storage your device has:.

In terms of availability, Google says a supported device will “automatically download the 3D emoji when it’s on Wi-Fi and charging.”.

At this time, there isn’t a way to force download the emoji.

Google announced 3D emoji in May, with the newly introduced design shipping on the Pixel 11 in August. It has since arrived on older Pixel devices.

In terms of OEM availability, Google explicitly claims “Samsung devices use a proprietary emoji font and do not receive the 3D font update.” Additionally:.

This is also true for third-party messaging apps, such as WhatsApp, who use their own emoji fonts rather than relying on your device’s system font.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

In a recent development, weekly. Free. One click to leave.

Industry observers note that A short clip can help a project in different ways. It can show an idea you have not filmed, put an existing design in motion, or give an announcement something to look at. The same approach will not work if the clip needs to demonstrate a real feature or show exactly what happened. Before choosing a generator, decide what the viewer needs to learn from the shot.

It has been revealed that this article uses Kling 4.0 as a worked example, but the decision process applies to any AI video generator. It covers how these tools turn prompts and images into video, how Kling 4.0 and a few alternatives differ, how to choose a starting mode, how to add exact text and branding outside the generated clip with a short ffmpeg script, and when real footage is the better choice. Feature details come from each vendor’s own pages at the time of writing and change often, so confirm current terms before you initiative a production.

Sources indicate that ● Generated video is best for imagined shots. It suits concepts, backgrounds and early explorations, not instructions or faithful records.

● Your starting material decides the mode. A written idea, a reference image or a pair of opening and closing frames each call for a different input.

It has been revealed that ● Keep exact wording out of the generated clip. Titles, dates and logos belong on separate layers in an editor.

● Tools differ on control, cost and licensing. Compare inputs, length, resolution, credits and terms before you commit.

Industry observers note that ● Always review. Watch the whole clip at its final size and check it against the real product or design.

In a recent development, most current systems extend diffusion models across time. A model learns to turn noise into a coherent set of frames guided by a prompt, and sometimes by an image or a clip. The research paper Video Diffusion Models describes this extension from images to video. The practical consequences are easy to observe.

● The prompt describes change over time. One visible change and one camera instruction usually work better than a long list of actions.

● Reference material steers but does not lock. A picture can suggest shape and colour without guaranteeing an exact match.

In a recent development, ● Longer clips give more room for drift. Faces, logos and fine text are the first things to change between frames.

Industry observers note that ● Cost grows with length and resolution. Most hosted tools charge credits per second, so short previews are cheaper than full shots.

Industry observers note that if you only have an idea, start with text. For a short announcement, you might ask for a band of light to move across a wall of coloured tiles. No one needs to recognise a particular wall, so the model can decide how it looks. Give it one visible change and a clear view of the subject. A prompt such as Soft morning light travels slowly across a wall of blue ceramic tiles. Fixed camera, no lettering is enough to see whether the idea works.

Industry observers note that if you already have an illustration or a photo, reference mode gives you another starting point. Suppose you want a short concept clip for a desk accessory that only exists as a drawing. The picture can show the general shape and colour while the prompt describes the view you want. A video reference can help when it is the motion that is hard to explain, such as a slow camera slide. Say what each asset is meant to guide, and do not add a clip just because you have one.

It has been revealed that use keyframes when a particular view matters at a particular moment. Start with an opening image. If a short reveal also needs to end with the object facing forward, add an ending image to show that view. That is different from a reference image that mainly reveals what the object looks like. Neither method guarantees an exact match, so check the result rather than assuming the uploaded picture has locked the design.

Recent findings suggest that no single tool fits every project. The table summarizes what each option’s own page states, and “not stated” means the page did not say, not that the feature is absent.

Reading the table: hosted studios such as the one on JXP are the quickest way to test an idea and need no setup, but you pay per second and work within their supported inputs. Kling’s own site is the place to check announcements and API options directly, since its page indicates little about durations or resolution. Runway positions its models for motion quality and prompt following, while Google’s Gemini API video documentation suits teams building generation into their own products. The Diffusers video guide covers open-source pipelines for developers who want local control and are ready to manage GPUs and licences.

Trying an idea before making it. An illustrator might want to see how an imagined landscape feels when the light changes. A quick clip gives the team something to discuss: is the change visible, and does it happen at the right pace? It does not need to be the final animation to answer those questions.

Showing a product concept. A rotating view or a slow camera move can help people discuss how a design might be presented. It is useful early, when the shape and lighting are still being explored. Once the clip represents a product someone can buy, the standard changes. If a port moves or a button appears that the real product does not have, it is the wrong clip for that job.

It has been revealed that making a short visual for a post. A few seconds of moving colour can give an event announcement or a project patch a distinctive opening. Put the name, date and other exact wording in your editor so they are readable and easy to change. The background only needs to support the message. If it competes with the text, use less movement or keep the background still.

Industry observers note that generated video is unreliable at lettering, so add titles in an editor or with a script. The command below overlays a title on a generated background and then checks the file properties. It assumes you already have a clip named background.mp4 and ffmpeg installed.

-vf "drawtext=text='Launch Night | 12 March':fontcolor=white:fontsize=64:x=(w-text_w)/2:y=(h-text_h)/2:box=1:boxcolor=black@0.35:boxborderw=24" \.

-c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -an announcement.mp4.

ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 \.

-show_entries stream=width,height,r_frame_rate,duration \.

-of default=noprint_wrappers=1 announcement.mp4.

It has been revealed that because the text lives in the command, you can reuse the same background for three events by changing one string. The font may need to be set with a fontfile option on some systems. This is the practical version of keeping the moving background in one file and the editable details in another.

Recent findings suggest that if people will follow the clip as instructions, use real footage or a screen recording for the steps. A convincing shot of an app is not proof that a button is in the right place. A generated close-up of a product is not a reliable way to show how its parts fit. You can still use an imagined opening, but make the switch to the real demonstration clear.

It has been revealed that think about revisions, too. If your team expects to adjust the same title, logo or date every week, put those elements on separate layers in an editor. And if the only movement you need is a slow zoom on an approved picture, apply that zoom directly. There is no reason to risk changing the picture when a simple edit will do.

This matters when someone else will maintain the video. A reusable announcement template is easier to hand over if the moving background is one file and the event details are editable. If the team likes the movement but needs three versions with different dates, they can reuse the same clip. If every change calls for a newly introduced generation, the time you saved on the first version may disappear on the second.

Industry observers note that the Kling 4.0 video generator on JXP at the moment offers 720p and 1080p settings and clip lengths from 3 to 30 seconds. According to its page, reference mode accepts up to 10 images and 5 videos, keyframe mode takes a first frame, middle frames and an optional last frame, and credits are charged per second with a higher rate at 1080p. For a first attempt, choose the frame shape you plan to use and make the clip only as long as it needs to be. Check the displayed credit cost before generating, because a short preview can tell you whether the direction works before you spend on a longer shot.

Decide what a good result looks like before you generate it. For the tile background, you need to see the light move without distracting from the words you will add. For a product concept, check whether the shape stays recognisable as the viewpoint changes. Watch the whole clip at the size the audience will see it. If the shot misses the point, revise one thing at a time: the motion, the framing or the source image.

According to recent reports, ● Read the licence. JXP’s page lists a commercial use license on each plan and says outputs are for creative and lawful use, with the user responsible for reviewing them. Other tools have different terms.

● Do not misrepresent products or events. A generated clip should not suggest features or footage that do not exist.

● Consider provenance. C2PA is an open standard for Content Credentials that records where content came from and how it was edited, and some tools support it.

Industry observers note that ● Disclose where required. Follow platform and advertising rules on labelling AI-generated or altered content.

● Fine text, logos, hands and fast motion can drift or flicker between frames.

● Reference images and keyframes steer the result but do not guarantee an exact match.

● Vendor specifications, such as resolution and length, can differ between a model announcement and a particular platform.

● Credit costs and blueprint terms change, so check them on the day you generate.

● Long or exact sequences are often cheaper and safer to film than to generate.

Short imagined shots, concept clips and moving backgrounds, where some details can be left open and the clip is reviewed before use.

Use text when you only have an idea, reference mode when you have a picture or clip to guide the look, and keyframes when specific views matter at specific moments.

It has been revealed that not reliably. Use real footage or a screen recording for instructions and demonstrations.

No. Hosted studios, vendor sites, developer APIs and open-source pipelines all exist. Compare supported inputs, length, resolution, cost and licensing against your project.

Kling 4.0 is a good candidate when the missing piece is an imagined shot and you can describe what it needs to do. Pick one such shot, try it, and put it next to the material you already have, and compare at least one alternative before you commit. If the project needs exact instructions or a faithful record, use the real thing. A useful first result is one that does its job in the edit, not simply one that looks impressive on its own.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After the better part of 7 years, Samsung’s mobile division has a fresh chief and it’s Choi Won-Joon, who is already off to a great start with the successful launch of Galaxy Z Fold 8.

Sources indicate that in an announcement today, Samsung confirmed some shuffling of its executive team, most notably with the end of TM Roh’s tenure as the head of Samsung’s MX business unit. In other words, there’s a upcoming captain at the helm for Samsung’s mobile division, and it’s Choi Won-Joon.

Won-Joon has been the Chief Operating Officer of Samsung’s MX unit since March of 2025, and more recently oversaw the launch of Galaxy S26 and Galaxy Z Fold 8, appearing on stage at both launch events and in behind-the-scenes meetings with the press.

Choi Won-joon, Head of the MX Business Unit at Samsung Electronics’ DX Division, has held positions such as Head of the Next-Generation Product Development Team, Head of the Strategic Product Development Team, and Head of Development at the MX Business Unit. Since being appointed President and Chief Operating Officer (COO) of the MX Business Unit in March 2025, he has led the successive successes of the Galaxy S26 and Z Fold 8. Based on the know-how accumulated while leading the development of the Galaxy series for a long time, he is expected to lead innovation in foldable phones, on-device AI, and wearables.

TM Roh isn’t leaving the company, but will drop his responsibilities in the mobile division. He remains one of two CEOs at Samsung alongside Jeon Young-hyun.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following this week’s casting of Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond, Google Search has already added a clever little Easter egg to celebrate the announcement.

Sources indicate that amazon announced on November 16 that actor Robert Pattinson will take on the role of James Bond, though his first film does not yet have a firm release window. Denis Villeneuve, best known for the Dune trilogy, will direct the movie.

Commemorating the casting, Google Search has added a upcoming Easter egg when you search for “Robert Pattinson.”.

Sources indicate that the actor’s results page now shakes the highlighted photos before dropping a lemon peel garnish on top, a cheeky reference to Bond’s “shaken, not stirred” martini order. It’s a clever little Easter egg, and a timely one too as it appeared not long after the casting was unveiled.
